# Reprojection focus and click-away order in grid editing

## Context

This is a leaf of #18762. It was split from #18863 on 2026-09-18, when PR #18912 delivered that ticket's AC-3 (the edited cell stays selected after an Enter commit) and AC-4 (an invalid draft keeps the editor). #18912 resolves the narrowed #18863. This ticket carries the two ACs it left open, word for word.

@neo-opus-vega built AC-1's first half, where the editor takes focus back when focus was in it at suspension, and it works. She reverted it because the second half had no sound signal, and shipping half an AC was not an option.

## The Problem

**AC-1's second half.** A reprojected editor must not take focus back when a newer gesture moved focus away while the edit was suspended. The attempt read `view.containsFocus` at reprojection time, and it looked stuck at `true` after focus had gone to a plain element outside the app.

It is not stuck. Measured on `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing`, real Chromium:
- Setup: suspend an edit (edit `c3` of record 3, scroll the pooled grid until the editor leaves the DOM, focus falls to `grid.View`), then click `#grid-cell-editing-outside`.
- Read immediately after the click: `true`.
- Read 150 ms later, and on every read after: `false`. 3 runs of 3.
- The plain case (a cell click, then the outside button, by click or `.focus()`) behaves the same.

`manager.Focus` defers a focusout's leave by `maxFocusInOutGap` (50 ms), so that a focusout followed by a focusin becomes a move. `containsFocus` therefore reports the state from before the gesture for that gap plus a worker round trip. A read in the same tick as the gesture cannot tell a click-away from nothing happening.

**AC-2.** A click on another cell while editing must commit, then select, in that order. That order has no event-level witness yet.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/Focus.mjs`: `onFocusout()` waits `maxFocusInOutGap` before `focusLeave()`, and a focusin inside the gap becomes `focusMove()`. `focusMove()` with no common component leaves the whole old path, so focus going to a non-Neo element does clear the path, one gap later.
- `grid.plugin.CellEditing` reprojects a suspended session when its cell renders again (`onBodyRender`, #18898). Suspension leaves focus on `grid.View`.
- `main.DomEvents` forwards `focusin` and `focusout` for every element, Neo or not.

## The Fix

> **Corrected 2026-09-18 (author), while implementing:** the first version of this section prescribed recording the View's `focusLeave` from suspension on, as "event-driven, so the 50 ms gap cannot fool it". That was wrong. `manager.Focus#setComponentFocus` sets `containsFocus` and fires `focusLeave` in the same call, so an event lags the gap exactly as the flag does. It is also more fragile: a suspension whose `revertFocus` lands after the gap reads as the View being left.

The suspension blur marks the session: the editor's leave while it is not embodied (a scroll), or the leave a lock change owes, registers a one-shot `mounted` listener. The editor's own reprojected mount then takes focus back only while `view.containsFocus` still holds. Read there, it is correct for every reprojection that lands after the gap, which a scroll or a lock change following a gesture always does.

For AC-2, witness the order the plugin already has: its commit and the cell selection, recorded by event.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1**: a reprojected editor takes focus back when focus was in it at suspension, and does not when a newer gesture moved focus. The first arm fails first on `dev`. The second arm moves focus both inside the app and to a non-Neo element, and restores after the 50 ms gap has passed, so a same-tick read cannot pass it.
- [ ] **AC-2**: a click on another cell while editing commits, then selects, in that order, witnessed at the event level.
- [ ] **AC-3**: each arm is killed by a named mutation recorded in the PR.

## Out of Scope

- The ACs #18912 delivers.
- Changing `maxFocusInOutGap`, or making `containsFocus` synchronous. The deferral is what turns a focusout plus focusin into a move.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Reading `containsFocus` in the tick of the gesture.** It is correct one gap later, and a same-tick read is how this AC was first missed. Recording the View's `focusLeave` does not avoid the gap either, because it fires with the flag.
- ⛔ **Fixing the lag in `manager.Focus`.** Every island (pickers, menus, the editor) relies on a move not being a leave.

- #18863 (split from; its PR is #18912) · #18762 (epic) · #18898 (`onBodyRender`)
